contradictions.fact: Name/identity of the high camp the climb starts from

claims.says: Goodell Creek trailhead to Terror Camp in Crescent Creek Basin
Alpine start (~4:00 AM) from Terror Camp
Terror Basin camp
This is the SEPARATE Crescent Creek cross-country zone, not Terror Basin

contradictions.why: The start is given as 'Terror Camp', while the camp list presents Terror Basin camp and Crescent Creek Basin camp as separate places in separate permit zones, so a climber can't tell which camp is meant.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The approach places 'Terror Camp' in Crescent Creek Basin (bivy[0], elev 6050), so the start should name Crescent Creek Basin camp.

contradictions.fact: Number of gully rappels on the descent

claims.says: West Ridge notch rappels (2x ~30m) then a loose gully with several more rappels back down to Crescent Creek Cirque
descend a chossy, steep-snow gully with an overhanging chockstone rappel back into Crescent Creek Cirque

contradictions.why: RAPPELS says 'several more' gully rappels, but the displayed descent names a single chockstone rappel in the gully.

contradictions.fact: Crux grade of the knife-edge finish

claims.says: Grade IV, 5.8
crux 5.8+ per the published account of the 1985 extension
an extended/left-side finish variant was climbed by Stoddard July 14-17, 1985 and is known as "North Face, Left Side" (5.8+)

contradictions.why: The route's own finish pitch quotes a 5.8+ crux taken from the 1985 variant, which fa describes as a separate line, while every grade column says 5.8.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The fa field treats the 1985 5.8+ finish as a separate variant, so the pitch note should not quote it as this route's crux.

contradictions.fact: Length of the low-fifth crest section

claims.says: climbing thousands of feet of low-fifth to 5.8 rock
Thousands of feet of low-fifth simul-climbing along the crest

contradictions.why: The prose says 'thousands of feet' of low-fifth, but that row is 304.8 m (1,000 ft) and the whole route is only 762 m (2,500 ft).
contradictions.internal_resolution: length_m and the pitch rows add up to 762 m, so the 'thousands of feet' prose is the overstatement.

contradictions.fact: Which climbers path the approach uses from the Terror Creek cairn

claims.says: Do not continue straight past the cairn; that fainter track follows Terror Creek toward Crescent Creek Basin and is a separate (and notoriously brushier) approach. Instead take the hard right and start up the steep, well-beaten Terror Basin boot path
follow the old road bed then the Terror Creek climber's path — a notoriously brushy, hard-to-follow route with a creek crossing — up to a bench camp around 6,000 ft
out the Terror Creek climber's path to the trailhead
the unmarked turnoff onto the Terror Basin climbers' path

contradictions.why: The approach says not to take the Terror Creek track, calling it a separate and brushier line, but the itinerary sends Day 1 and the hike-out up that path and describes it the way the approach describes the path to avoid.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The approach, approach_variants[0] and waypoints[1] all use the well-beaten Terror Basin boot path, so the itinerary (and timing.sectionBreakdown notes copied from it) is the outlier.

contradictions.fact: Line from Terror Basin to the base of the North Face (waypoints)

claims.says: Terror Glacier crossing
Crevasse hazard traversing toward the north face base
The technical start of the North Face is reached from the Crescent Creek Basin camp by crossing the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col and descending the Mustard Glacier into McMillan Cirque
cross the Otto-Himmel col and traverse below the Twin Spires and the Rake to reach the base of the North Face

contradictions.why: The waypoints go from Terror Basin across the Terror Glacier to the face, 1 mile, with no Barrier, Crescent Creek Basin or Otto-Himmel col. The approach and itinerary reach the face over the Otto-Himmel col and the Mustard Glacier.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The approach, approach_variants[0].baseFinding, the itinerary and the gear (Mustard Glacier) all agree, so the waypoint list is the outlier.

contradictions.fact: Distance from the trailhead to the Terror Creek cairn

claims.says: along Goodell Creek for roughly 4 to 4.5 miles — gentle grade, easy walking — to a stone-cairn/arrow junction near 1,700 ft
The roughly four miles of overgrown roadbed to the cairn

contradictions.why: The cairn waypoint is at 3.5 mi, while the approach puts it at 4-4.5 mi.

claims.says: the standard high camp is in a gravelly, wildflower basin about 400 ft below and beyond the saddle, around 5,700 ft
up to a bench camp around 6,000 ft
Reach the 6,000 ft basin below the Southern Pickets

contradictions.why: The Day 1 camp is given as 5,700 ft in the approach and 6,000 ft in the itinerary, 300 ft apart.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The waypoint and bivy both say 5,800, and the approach says about 400 ft below the 6,200 ft saddle.

claims.says: A 15+ hr day
one very long (14-15 hr) technical day

contradictions.why: The schedule runs from 2:30 AM to about 8:00 PM, which is 17.5 hours, but the day is listed as 14 hours and described as 14-15 or '15+' hours.

contradictions.fact: Descent entry notch (Terror-Rake notch vs notch north of the Chopping Block)

claims.says: downclimb/scramble the West Ridge crest westward toward the low notch between Terror and The Rake, where a large chockstone marks the top of the descent gully system

Do not rappel into the low notch north of the sub-peak known as the Chopping Block — the correct line into Crescent Creek Basin is about 100 yards north of that notch, at a flat, bivy-site shelf on the ridge

contradictions.why: The same descent text puts the gully entry at the chockstone in the Terror-Rake notch and also 100 yards north of a notch by the Chopping Block, which is a separate peak about 2 km south.

claims.says: has been reported reachable from near the summit — a call from the summit area was critical in a 2009 rescue
No cell coverage in the Pickets.

contradictions.why: COMMS reports a signal near the summit, while EMERGENCY says there is no coverage in the Pickets.
contradictions.internal_resolution: comms gives a specific reported instance, so emergency.notes should say coverage is unreliable rather than none.

claims.says: total approach elevation gain to basecamp is nearly 6,000 ft

contradictions.why: gain_ft equals the approach gain to camp alone, but the summit day adds about 2,100 ft more (6,050 to 8,151), so total ascent is about 8,000+ ft.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The approach gain (about 6,000) plus camp-to-summit (about 2,100) gives about 8,100, so gain_ft 6000 is too low.

contradictions.fact: Number of rappels above the notch

claims.says: Two or three rappels in the gully, plus one or two above the notch, get parties down
the summit tower is downclimbed or a short section rappelled back to the notch off existing sling anchors. One short step, not a sequence.
Downclimb the summit tower or rap a short section

contradictions.why: The base-finding text gives 'one or two' rappels above the notch, then says it is one short step, not a sequence.
contradictions.internal_resolution: rappels, descent and descent_text all describe one short optional rappel above the notch.

claims.says: Early start from Terror Camp
Day 1: approach to Terror Camp/Crescent Creek Basin
It is not the camp you climb Terror from

contradictions.why: 'Terror Camp' reads as the Terror Basin camp, which the bivy list says is not the camp you climb Terror from. The climb starts from Crescent Creek Basin.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The beta and approach both start from Crescent Creek Basin.

claims.says: N/A - non-glaciated summer route
Potential avalanche exposure on approach slopes—assess stability in spring; afternoon warming increases risk; early start essential

contradictions.why: SAFETY rates avalanche N/A for the Jul-Sep route, while KNOWN HAZARDS lists avalanche exposure on the approach slopes, framed for a spring trip the route's season excludes.

claims.says: Ice axe & crampons (glacier approach via Crescent Creek Basin/Mustard Glacier)
Glacier travel gear for the Crescent Creek Basin/Mustard Glacier approach
Do not use the north side of the col as an escape — it drops onto the Mustard Glacier
From that camp, snow and small glacier slopes lead northwest in about an hour to the Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col

contradictions.why: The gear fields say the approach uses the Mustard Glacier, but the approach stays on the south (Crescent Creek) side, and the bail and descent say to avoid the Mustard Glacier.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The approach, descent_text and bail all keep the route south of the col, so the Mustard Glacier mention in the gear fields is wrong.

contradictions.fact: Scramble grade of the standard finish

claims.says: Class 4 (a 5.7 variation exists on the north side of the summit blocks)
Class 4 (or 5.7 variation on the north side)
accounts consistently call the peak class 3 and describe it as one of the few Southern Picket summits that is not fifth class

contradictions.why: The grade columns say Class 4, while the climbing-route text says accounts 'consistently' call it class 3.

claims.says: the near-identical Goodell Creek / Terror Basin / Barrier approach to Mount Terror is recorded at 20 miles and 10,000 ft round trip

contradictions.why: dist_km is 16.1 km (10 mi) on an out-and-back, but the approach says the near-identical trip is 20 mi round trip. dist_km looks one-way, shown as the trip distance.

claims.says: N/A - non-glaciated summer rock route
approach crosses glaciated terrain near Ottohorn-Himmelhorn col requiring rope for glacier travel
Likely crevasse hazard on the glacier/snow approach into the Crescent Creek basin during early season
glacier travel and crevasse rescue for the approach (Crescent Creek basin)
Ice axe for early-season snow

contradictions.why: The row calls the route non-glaciated, yet says the approach needs a rope for glacier travel and crevasse-rescue skills. The gear list has only an ice axe.

contradictions.fact: Time from camp to the Otto-Himmel col

claims.says: +2 hr
About an hour above camp
parties have done it from the col in roughly an hour round trip

contradictions.why: The schedule allows 2 hours to the col, but the col waypoint says it is about an hour above camp.

contradictions.fact: Height from the col to the summit

claims.says: Route is approximately 500–700 vertical feet from col to summit.

contradictions.why: The col (7,400) and summit (7,840) waypoints are 440 ft apart, not the 500-700 ft the beta gives.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The waypoints and approach agree on a 7,400 ft col, so the beta's 500-700 ft is the outlier.

contradictions.fact: Driving direction to Goodell Creek Road

claims.says: From Sedro-Woolley/Marblemount, follow WA-20 east past Newhalem; Goodell Creek Road turns off near the Goodell Creek Campground
reached via the gravel road that forks off Hwy 20 across from Newhalem
across SR-20 from Newhalem

contradictions.why: The drive note says to go east past Newhalem, while the approach and trailhead put the turn across from Newhalem, which a driver from the west reaches before Newhalem.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The approach and both trailhead descriptions put the road across from Newhalem.

contradictions.fact: Whether the zone permit can be reserved

claims.says: reserve on Recreation.gov or walk-up at the Marblemount Wilderness Information Center
Reserve on Recreation.gov, then get the permit by email or in person
About 60% of sites can be reserved in advance via Recreation.gov
It is NOT on the short list of zones reservable in advance, so it is WALK-UP ONLY
Cross-country zone permit from the Wilderness Information Center

contradictions.why: The permit fields tell climbers to reserve on Recreation.gov, but the Terror Basin camp says the zone is walk-up only and cannot be reserved.
contradictions.internal_resolution: bivy[3] is the zone-specific statement, and every sibling Southern Pickets row in this batch says Terror Basin and Crescent Creek are walk-up only, so the reservable wording is the outlier.

claims.says: free NPS backcountry permit required for any overnight camping
needs a free backcountry wilderness permit
$10 per person (charged mid-May through early October; no fee October-mid-May) plus a $6 non-refundable processing fee

contradictions.why: The trailhead waypoint calls the permit free, but ACCESS lists $10 per person plus $6.
contradictions.internal_resolution: access.fees is the detailed, dated fee schedule, so 'free' is only true outside the mid-May to early-October season.

contradictions.fact: Where the Day 1 camp is and how much the day gains

claims.says: dropping to a flat camp around 5,800 ft. It's a brutal, sustained ~4,000+ ft grind
Cross the Barrier ridge into Stump Hollow/Crescent Creek Basin
the standard high camp for the South Route
to a high camp on the Stump Hollow ridge below the peak

contradictions.why: The Day 1 note calls it a ~4,000+ ft day but lists 5,700 ft of gain. The itinerary camps in Terror Basin and reaches Stump Hollow on Day 2, while the waypoint and beta make Stump Hollow the high camp.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The approach ('well over 5,000 ft of gain to camp') agrees with gainFt 5700, so '~4,000+' is the error. Which camp is meant needs a decision.

claims.says: ~6.5 mi and ~5,700 ft each way to camp

contradictions.why: dist_km (6.5 mi) is the one-way distance to camp, while the itinerary totals 16 mi, so the stats and the header would show different trip distances.

claims.says: Grade III, low 5th class
an option for parties wanting more technical climbing than the standard Class 3 west-side scramble
West-side Class 3 scramble tops out on the true summit
3rd-4th class with a few moves of low 5th (unrated)

contradictions.why: The grade pill says low fifth class, while a pro tip and the summit waypoint call the standard line a Class 3 scramble.
contradictions.internal_resolution: The grade, rock_grade, beta, waypoints[5] and approach_variants all include low-fifth moves, so 'Class 3 scramble' understates it.

contradictions.why: The schedule runs from 3:30 AM to 5:00 PM, which is 13.5 hours, but the day and timing.summitTimeHrs say 12.

claims.says: $10/person/night + $6 nonrefundable fee as of March 2024
